Date: 2027-03-07T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Annual Planning: target bands & scenario ladder — alignment request

Team —

We need to lock the top-level targets and scenario bands for FY28 so product, sales, and CS can proceed with QBR narratives and resource planning. Goal for this thread: agree on 1) high/expected/low revenue target bands, 2) key assumptions for the scenario ladder (hiring, win rates, pricing pressure), and 3) a lightweight timeline for two workshops (targets & scenarios; resourcing stress test).

Proposed timeline (suggest edits):
- Mar 15: Targets & Scenario Workshop (lead: Strategy)
- Mar 16: Resourcing / Capacity Stress Test (lead: People + CS)
- Mar 22: Draft targets circulated to execs

Ask: please reply with your top 3 risks/assumptions that should move the bands and any hard constraints from your area by end of day Tue (Mar 9). If you can, attach any spreadsheets or model snippets.

Im attaching a lightweight planning framework to get the ball rolling.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber | VP, Strategy & Go-to-Market
Redwood Inference

Attachment: FY28_planning_framework.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-03-07T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Annual Planning: target bands & scenario ladder — alignment request

Jonas —

Thanks for kicking this off. Quick reads: I agree with the workshop cadence, but two asks from my side: 

1) Shift the Targets workshop 90 minutes earlier to accommodate EMEA leadership (we have several cross-region owners) — proposed 11:00 PT.
2) Ill need AOP baseline from Finance (ACME contact included) and a band that isolates pricing/headcount variability.

Top 3 assumptions from infra/ops lens:
- GPU supply curve stabilizes in Q3 (if delayed, cost per token moves +12–18%)
- Enterprise procurement cycle shortens by 8 weeks if we provide Dedicated migration kits
- Quantization/optimized kernels adoption rate: 30% of requests by Q4 (cost delta matters)

If Marissa has a template for scenario math, thatll speed us up.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Chief Operating Officer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Annual Planning: target bands & scenario ladder — alignment request

Adding the finance view and a lightweight model. I attached two files: scenario_templates.docx (narrative + template) and FY28_planning_framework.xlsx (with three prefilled bands: conservative / base / stretch).

Highlights from the prefill:
- Base: $117.5M ARR (assumes current funnel conversion; 20% enterprise churn reduction from improved onboarding)
- Stretch: $142M ARR (assumes pricing mix shift + larger ACVs from Dedicated deals)
- Conservative: $98M ARR (assumes slower procurement cycle and 15% lower net new bookings)

Key assumption that moves bands: enterprise deal cadence — a 20% change in average ACV moves base by ~6 points.

I also included a simple sensitivity sheet that we can use live in the workshop.

Attachments:
- FY28_planning_framework.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
- scenario_templates.docx (doc stub)

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Finance, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Quick note — I like the two-workshop approach. A few practicals for QBR-ready outputs:
- Keep the initial targets slide to 1 page (topline + 3 bullets of key assumptions)
- Include an "owner + ask" column next to each assumption so the exec read is actionable
- OKR check-in cadence: monthly health + a mid-Q check (June) to trigger contingency plans

Ill draft a 1-pager template and drop it in the Drive folder.

Folks —

Two flags from CS that should land before we finalize bands: 
1) Capacity risk: current onboarding throughput will cap new enterprise seat activations in Q2 unless we add two additional onboarding specialists. I ran a short model; attaching a PDF with run rates.
2) Renewal timing: a cluster of large customers have renewals in late Q3 — if those slip, base could move down ~4–5 points.

Suggested mitigation: schedule the Resourcing / Capacity Stress Test and include a hiring delta column in the sensitivity sheet. Ive put a short note in the Drive folder.

Attachment: cs_capacity_stress_test.pdf (pdf stub)

—Monica
Monica Patel | Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

All — thanks for the fast turn. Consolidating decisions and next steps: 

Decisions
- Keep the two-workshop structure. Targets workshop will be 2027-03-15 11:00 PT (1.5h) — well invite EMEA leads.
- Resourcing / Capacity Stress Test will be 2027-03-16 09:00 PT (1h). Monica to lead and bring the CS run-rate PDF.
- Use Marissa's Base/Stretch/Conservative bands as the starting point; Finance will surface AOP baselines during the workshop.

Immediate actions (owners)
- Marissa: finalize sensitivity tab and circulate updated spreadsheet by Mar 12. (attachment: FY28_planning_framework.xlsx)
- Vivek: prepare an ops assumptions slide (GPU supply, kernel adoption cadence) by Mar 12.
- Monica: lead the Resourcing stress test; add hiring deltas to the sensitivity sheet by Mar 14.
- Stephanie: draft the 1-page QBR slide template and add owner+ask column; drop in Drive by Mar 11.

Links & notes
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-planning-FY28
- HubSpot note for ACME finance baseline: HUBSPOT: contact-4321
- Jira ticket for workshop logistics: PLANNING-78

Ill send calendar invites once Marissa confirms the spreadsheet timing. If there are objections to the dates/times above, flag them by EOD Fri (Mar 12).

Thanks — lets get this into a QBR-ready shape.

Jonas
